questions.template: Electricity only flows when the circuit is…?
questions.hint: Think of a racetrack — cars need the whole track.
questions.explain: Current needs an unbroken loop from the battery, around, and back.

questions.template: Which of these needs electricity to work?
questions.explain: Bulbs glow when current flows through them.

questions.template: What does a switch do in a circuit?
questions.explain: A switch closes the loop (on!) or breaks it (off!).

questions.template: Which material lets electricity flow through it?
questions.explain: Metals like copper are conductors; plastic and wood are insulators.

questions.template: Why are plug casings made of plastic?
choices: Plastic is an insulator — it keeps us safe
questions.hint: It's about what electricity CANNOT go through.
questions.explain: Insulators like plastic stop current reaching our hands.

questions.template: A bulb won't light. The battery is fine. What's the likely problem?
questions.hint: Check every connection — is the loop truly closed?
questions.explain: Any break — a loose wire, an open switch — stops the whole circuit.
